Question: For integers \(k\) and \(n\) such that \(1\le k\lt n,\) let \[ \binom nk=\frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}. \] Then \(\left(\frac{n-2k-1}{k+1}\right)\binom nk\) is an integer

Choices.B:
for all even values of \(k\) and \(n,\) but not for all \(k\)
and \(n\)
Choices.C:
for all odd values of \(k\) and \(n,\) but not for all \(k\)
and \(n\)
Choices.D:
if \(k=1\) or \(n-1,\) but not for all odd values of \(k\) and
\(n\)
Choices.E:
if \(n\) is divisible by \(k,\) but not for all even values of
\(k\) and \(n\)
